blocks.p: Rei walked back to Akabane through the wet morning and caught the Keihin-Tōhoku line south toward home. It was early, and the train was nearly empty. An old man sat across from him with a cloth bundle on his knees, tied at the top. Through the cloth Rei could see the shapes of fruit and a small bottle of sake, offerings for a family grave. A cleaner in white gloves moved down the car picking up a newspaper someone had left. The river smell was still in Rei's clothes.

He opened the soft cardboard folder on his knees. Behind the first pages of Gin's field profile, Tanizaki had tucked four sheets copied from Gin's archive. They came from a chapter headed The Masters. Gin had written them the way he wrote everything for the archive, plainly, for someone who would need them later. Tanizaki had added one yellow note of his own, stuck to the first sheet in his small square hand.

doc.title: The Masters. What the word means
lines: Masters are Vanguard-rank independents. The CVD files them as unreliable. They are unreliable for structural reasons. They choose their own cases. They need clearance time to stay stable at Vanguard. They take the long view of patterns. And every one of them paid a personal cost.

Most Masters paid for their capability with something specific. A relationship they could not keep while developing. A period of severe depletion that permanently changed their stability floor. Encounters that changed how they engage with entities.
The capability and the cost are the same thing.

The unreliability framing is a CVD framing. From the Masters' side, they are not unreliable. They are correctly managing a capability the institution does not know how to manage, and would manage badly if it could.
The three Vanguard practitioners I know directly are not manageable. I am including myself in this assessment.
Working rules. Do not deploy, consult. The exchange is real. Their cost is visible. Respect what they will not tell you. (G.U.)

blocks.p: The next three sheets were portraits of the three Masters Gin knew best. Each one gave the person's rank and gift, what they would do and what they would not, and what their power had cost them.

doc.title: Yamamoto Koji. The Archivist
lines: Vanguard rank. Clairsentience. Independent.

Former senior practitioner in the CVD Research Division. Left sixteen years ago, after the Division classified a large part of his entity taxonomy work and restricted its use in the field. He did not disagree with the research. He disagreed with the classification.

Keeps an independent archive of entity intelligence he has been building for twenty-two years. The most comprehensive private collection of entity documentation I am aware of. Lives in it, in a book-drowned flat near the building. The location is documented nowhere outside the archive itself.
Terms. He tells you what he knows, you tell him what you found, the exchange updates both archives. He has never charged money for a consultation.
He only takes cases that produce new entity knowledge. Standard possessions and routine clearances he passes to his network. People read this as refusal. It is efficiency.
The reading that takes a standard practitioner thirty minutes takes him the time it takes to walk around the perimeter of the location once.

What he cost himself. Two decades of institutional standing, access to the classified material he produced himself, and the relationships the departure ended. He does not appear to regret the departure. He appears to regret the material he cannot reach.

He has reviewed my case files three times in six years. Each time he told me what I had found before I finished describing it. He is the practitioner I have learned the most from in this field. (G.U.)

doc.title: Stuck to the Yamamoto page, in Tanizaki's hand
lines: Yamamoto holds an entry from twenty-two years ago. An encounter in Kita with a Duty-register demon working through a multi-spectrum host.
He did not know then what it was. He knows now. He has cross-referenced the signatures.
It is the first correct naming of that register as Duty anywhere in any record. The CVD instruments call it null-emotive. They are wrong.
It also holds the history of this thing in our district further back than any institutional file.
He will trade it for a true thing of the same weight. Never for money. Gin never brought him the trade. You might. T.

doc.title: Ishida Ryō. The Closer
lines: Vanguard rank. Telekinesis. Grid-adjacent.
Never registered. Forty-one. Born into a family with no practitioner history. Developed Telekinesis in early adolescence and found the Grid before any institution found him.
The CVD tried to recruit him three times. He declined each time. The fourth attempt, about eight years ago, produced an exchange with the assessor that became Grid legend. There has not been a fifth.

Takes Class B demon operations, thin-spot escalations the standard squads cannot manage, and structural membrane damage. Through the Grid only. No CVD coordination. He decides the approach, he does the primary work, and he does not take direction during operations.
He does not move objects. He moves the relationship between objects and the space they occupy. In a contested space, gravity, pressure and force become optional at his discretion.
Response time is hours to weeks. Urgency does not change it. Interesting problems get faster responses than simple ones.
What he cost himself. Isolation. Three separate Grid contacts have called him the loneliest person they know who does not appear to be aware of it. I have not asked him.
Two operations with him in six years. Standing near him in the field feels like standing near a change in how physics works in that one place. It is not comfortable. It is effective. (G.U.)

doc.title: Watanabe Sora. The Mediator
lines: Vanguard rank. Telepathy. Works with both the CVD and the Grid. Former Kairo.

A former Vessel Program operative. She shared her body with a contracted entity for four years and was released after the entity violated the contract terms. The exit was managed quietly. She kept her registration.
The only practitioner I know who developed Vanguard Telepathy after a Vessel Program exit.

She is the one you call when the demon can be talked to more effectively than removed. Her negotiations end in contracts, in voluntary departures, in entities that leave peacefully and do not come back. The outcomes are slower. They last longer.
She only takes cases where she judges negotiation is viable. She will not negotiate with an entity that has shown it cannot honour an agreement. She does not explain her refusals.

What she cost herself. The trust of someone who was never violated the way she was. She trusts entities more than most practitioners find comfortable. Her view is that contracts are real to entities, in ways the standard taxonomy does not admit.

Three possession cases with her over four years. She is also the one who spoke most directly about my own compromise, working inside the CVD while objecting to several of its programs. I have thought about what she said many times. I have not resolved it. (G.U.)

blocks.p: Under the Mediator's page was one more sheet. It was a photocopy of a CVD reference card with a red stamp in the corner, and Gin had written along its margin in pencil.

The card was about something Rei had never heard of. The CVD had a squad made of the dead. These were practitioners who had agreed, before they died, that their bodies could go on working afterwards. When they died, their souls went on to wherever the dead go. Then a demon was let into each empty body under a written contract, and the body kept working for the CVD. The card called it the Vessel Program. The squad's name was Kairo.

blocks.cap: A CVD squad in the field

doc.title: 廻路. Kairo. The Vessel Program Squad. Existence restricted. Need to know
lines: What it is. A squad operating under the Vessel Program. Former practitioners whose pre-mortem consent authorised continued operational use of their bodies after crossing. Their souls have crossed and taken their own death paths. The bodies continue, operated by contracted entities, under formal agreements monitored by the Program's oversight team.

The contract. Each entity has signed for a specific feeding register, specific behavioural parameters, no predatory escalation, cooperation with Program monitoring, and deployment only within agreed case types.

The entity receives physical presence in the living world. A body, sensation, the warmth and density of embodied existence that entities who remember life often want back. The CVD receives operational assets it cannot recruit any other way.
Contracts are monitored monthly. Drift is flagged and addressed.

Why demons can honour contracts. Demons are malicious by nature. But malice and intelligence do not rule out rational self-interest. A demon offered something it values more than what it could take by force will sometimes accept. The body is the offer. The terms are the price.
Function. Kairo is deployed on possession cases because its members recognise possession from the inside. They have caught possessions that standard assessment missed.

doc.title: Gin's pencil, down the margin of the Kairo card
lines: One case worked with Kairo. Usami Hinata, twenty-four, an urban-sociology graduate student who gave pre-mortem consent. Usami is dead. The body is run by a Class C love-register demon that gave its operational name as Ren.

Ren chose the Vessel Program over the Axis at the moment of crossing. Consistent contract compliance since transfer, eighteen months ago. Handles civilian interface. The warmth makes interview subjects comfortable.

Ren reads the register of anything within ten metres, other demons included. Lives in Kōenji, works part-time at a bakery, keeps Usami's white mug with the blue stripe. What is left of Usami is the thing Ren holds on to.
His line, when I asked how it works. "Two of us in here. He does the talking. I do the wanting."
Ren is not a liar. The most ethically straightforward entity contract I have seen. The arrangement appears genuine on both sides.
The entity seems to find the work meaningful, the way entities with enough sustenance and the right expression do. I did not expect to write that sentence about a demon. (G.U.)

blocks.p: Rei read the last line twice. Then the train pulled into Ōji, the short departure melody began to play on the platform, and he looked up. He closed the folder and sat with it on his knees until the doors began to close. Three people his brother had trusted, and every one of them had paid. A demon in Kōenji that kept a dead man's mug. And on the yellow note, a page twenty-two years old in a flat full of books, which might name the thing in Gin more truly than the whole CVD ever had. He got off the train one stop late and walked back under the cicadas.
